title: Gemstones and Puja: Finding Your Real Ishta Devta
sub: Notes on this standalone talk by Brajesh Gautam, The Anchor Of Life: reading life's early warning signs, the difference between Bhagwan, Ishwar, Ishta and Guru, the planets as a family, how manifestation works, and how a gemstone is chosen, worn and judged for quality.
desc: Complete notes on EP 20, Sanatan: Gemstone and Pooja Paath, by Brajesh Gautam: Bhagwan versus Ishwar versus Ishta versus Guru, the planetary family story, manifestation, Hanuman and Shiva worship risks, and how gemstones are chosen, worn and judged for quality, with video timestamps.
points: Read the signal before forcing the plan.
Repeated frustration is itself a sign to pause, not proof that you must push harder.
Bhagwan, Ishwar, Ishta and Guru are four different things.
The body, the soul within it, the one deity you personally rest on, and the guide who can switch your own light on.
The same deity can help or harm.
The speaker's claim is that worship only works when it reaches the right form, for your own chart, not any form that is simply popular.
The planets work like one household.
A father, mother, son, daughter, a servant, a suitor and two helpers, each relationship deciding which charity helps and which one backfires.
Manifestation needs the body to feel it, not just the mind to think it.
His test for whether something will actually land: can your body genuinely feel the outcome, not merely imagine it.
A gemstone is described as a hydrocarbon filter, not a charm.
It is said to draw in one planet's rays the way glasses bend light, matched to the specific planet that is afflicted in your chart.
Clarity matters more than carat size.
A small, flawless stone is said to outwork a larger, flawed one, the way a clean lens beats a scratched one.
